wreck_positions.quote: Additionally, for a number of reasons, AWOIS positions do not always agree with a charted position for a similar feature.
wreck_positions.source: NOAA Office of Coast Survey, on its wreck/obstruction records. The same notice states ENCs 'are the authoritative source of information about known or reported wrecks' — this dataset's wrecks are ENC extracts, and each feature carries its ENC source date (sordat) and source (sorind) so position vintage is visible per feature.

depths.statement: ENC depth values (valsou_m) are metres relative to chart datum; IHO S-57 requires ENC depth units to be metres (Use of the Object Catalogue for ENC). Per-feature vertical datum (VERDAT) is null in these extracts, so no per-feature datum claim is made; the US chart datum standard is mean lower low water.
depths.chart_datum_quote: Since 1980, chart datum has been implemented to mean lower low water for all marine waters of the United States, its territories, Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands.

pier_access.quote: PLEASE NOTE: CDFW cannot guarantee that individual piers, jetties, or breakwaters will be open to the public. The landowner may close these areas for safety, maintenance, or other reasons at any time.

reef_definition.quote: "Artificial reef" means manmade or natural objects intentionally placed in selected areas of the marine environment to duplicate those conditions that induce production of fish and invertebrates on natural reefs and rough bottoms, and that stimulate the growth of kelp or other midwater plant life which creates natural habitat for those species.
reef_definition.source: FindLaw mirror of the California Fish and Game Code, current as of January 1, 2026. leginfo.legislature.ca.gov disallows automated access, so the mirror is what was read and is what is cited.

corrections_note: Documented source-typo corrections applied to the records listed; each corrected record keeps the source's original wording in a source_-prefixed field and states why in correction_note. See _REEF_CORRECTIONS in the pipeline's spear_structures module.
category_label_corrections_note: NOAA ENC Direct publishes CATWRK/CATOBS as a 30-character label rather than an S-57 code. Two of those labels are artefacts of NOAA's value table rather than descriptions of the feature, and one is a real label cut off by the field's width. Each is corrected by a declared rule below; NO record is dropped for carrying one. A corrected record keeps NOAA's own string in source_catwrk (or source_catobs), which is also the `find` of the rule that corrected it in the list below. See _ENC_CATEGORY_LABEL_RULES in the pipeline's spear_structures module. The truncated label is the only rule that makes a label longer, and it is a QUOTATION: the full text comes from IHO's own S-57 CATWRK enumeration, captured on disk and declared in curated/enc_catwrk_labels_2026.json, which carries the standard's URL, the snapshot path and its sha256. The rule ships that citation with it, in its own `source` block.

category_label_corrections.why: NOAA ENC Direct publishes the S-57 non-dangerous-wreck category with the literal label 'non-dangerous wreck (test)'. Verified 2026-09-15 against the live enc_harbour/enc_approach/enc_coastal services: distinct CATWRK values nationwide are the same six on every band, and this is the only label any of them carries for that category — no plain 'non-dangerous wreck' value exists in the service. The '(test)' is NOAA's value table, not a statement about these wrecks, which carry ordinary ENC cell, chart and Local Notice to Mariners provenance. The label is corrected; the records ship.

One California row carries the literal three characters quote-space-quote as its CATWRK label. The obstruction half of the same service writes its unpopulated marker as a bare single space (1,103 rows), which `_clean` already reads as absence; this is that same blank, quoted. It is emptied rather than rewritten, because what category that wreck is is unknown — the record ships nameless and the app falls back to 'Wreck'. Nothing is invented to fill it.

category_label_corrections.find: wreck showing any portion of h
category_label_corrections.replace: wreck showing any portion of hull or superstructure
category_label_corrections.why: NOAA ENC Direct serves CATWRK as a 30-character string field with no coded-value domain, so it substitutes the S-57 label for the code and cuts it to the field width. 'wreck showing any portion of h' is that cut: it is exactly 30 characters, and it is the first 30 characters of exactly one value in IHO's own enumeration for this attribute — no other S-57 CATWRK label is even long enough to be truncated. The full label is quoted from that standard, not supplied from memory, and NOAA's own string is kept on every corrected record in source_catwrk. Declared in curated/enc_catwrk_labels_2026.json.
